# How a Concern Became a Law

<!-- STEP id="concerns" -->
## First, a Concern

The Right to Information (RTI) Act began with a concern about transparency and accountability. Citizens, journalists, civil society groups and elected representatives all raised it.

<!-- STEP id="committees" -->
## Then, Committees

Parliamentary committees examined these concerns. The discussions showed the need for a law to let citizens get information held by public authorities.

<!-- STEP id="debate" -->
## Then, Debate

Expert groups reviewed the proposal, Parliament debated it, and stakeholders were consulted. Elected representatives added safeguards for national security and administrative efficiency.

<!-- STEP id="in-force" -->
## 2005: Into Force

After Parliament passed it, the RTI Act came into force in **2005**. Citizens can now seek information from government departments.

Laws made in this way are called **legislation**.
